detailed_rationale:
Avalon Technologies is a fully integrated Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) provider offering end-to-end box-build solutions -- PCB design and assembly, sheet-metal fabrication, machining, cable/magnetics assembly, plastics, functional testing and logistics -- for high-value precision-engineered products. The last three reported quarters show a genuine, accelerating growth and margin trend: Q2 FY26 revenue Rs 382cr/PAT Rs 25cr (10% operating margin), Q3 FY26 Rs 418cr/Rs 33cr (11% margin), Q4 FY26 Rs 480cr/Rs 41cr (12% margin) -- steady sequential improvement in both scale and profitability, with Q4 revenue up roughly 40% YoY and TTM profit growth around 88%, broadly consistent with the quant row's rev growth1y of 46.0%.

A genuine data point worth surfacing rather than picking a single number to quote: the quant scorecard shows ROE of 25.7% (likely reflecting the recent, stronger quarters), while the company's own 3-year-average ROE is reported at just 11% -- a large gap that suggests the current profitability level is a relatively recent improvement rather than an established multi-year track record, and both figures are probably correct for their respective windows. Valuation is rich by any measure: PE of ~104-105x (consistent across both the quant row and this research) and 16.5x book value, with no dividend paid despite profitability -- fully consistent with a company still reinvesting through a capacity/capability build-out phase. Promoter holding has declined 6.85 percentage points over three years to 44.39% as of Jun-2026 -- a moderate, worth-noting but not alarming governance data point, common as early investors or promoters partially monetize post-listing.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold at both horizons (final_score_3y 64, final_score_1y 71). Fresh research confirms the growth and margin trend is real and improving quarter over quarter, which argues against Sell, but the extremely rich valuation (~104x earnings, 16.5x book) against a 3-year-average ROE of only 11% means this is priced almost entirely on the recent-quarter trend continuing -- not a statistically attractive add, so Hold is the right resting point.
summary: Avalon Technologies is a full-service electronics contract manufacturer (EMS) that has shown genuine, steady improvement over the last three quarters in both revenue growth (~40% YoY) and operating margin (10% to 12%). The company's three-year-average return on equity, however, is only about 11%, well below the much stronger recent-quarter figure, and the stock trades at a very rich ~104x earnings with no dividend. We rate it a Hold: real and improving momentum, but priced for a much longer track record of high returns than the company has actually delivered so far.
positive_para: Three consecutive quarters of sequential improvement in both revenue (Rs 382cr to Rs 418cr to Rs 480cr) and operating margin (10% to 11% to 12%) show genuine, broad-based operating momentum rather than a single lucky quarter; the EMS sector benefits from a real, multi-year India electronics-manufacturing policy tailwind (PLI, China+1 supply-chain diversification) that is structural rather than company-specific hype.
negative_para: The company's 3-year-average ROE of just 11% is well below the ~26% figure reflected in the most recent trailing data, meaning the current profitability level does not yet have an established multi-year track record -- the stock is being priced (at ~104x earnings, 16.5x book) almost entirely on the recent trend continuing, with very little room for a stumble; no dividend is paid despite profitability, and promoter holding has declined moderately (down ~6.85 points over three years) -- a governance data point worth monitoring rather than ignoring.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~104x trailing earnings, the valuation requires not just continuation of the recent 40%+ growth and improving-margin trend, but effectively a re-rating of the company's whole return-on-capital profile from its historical ~11% 3-year average toward the much stronger recent-quarter level on a sustained basis. That is a plausible outcome if the last three quarters mark a genuine structural improvement (capacity utilization, mix-shift to higher-value box-build work), but it is a large ask from a valuation that offers no margin of safety if the recent trend stalls.
